title: Taleem Initiative 2025
summary: Educational-kit support for students, with Amaana's donor update reporting support reaching 50 orphan children.
story:
Amaana's Taleem Initiative is an educational-kit distribution drive for students. The original campaign banner states that purpose, and the supplied archive places this edition in 2025.

A donor appreciation update thanks an individual supporter whose contribution, Amaana reports, helped bring joy to 50 orphan children. This is the campaign's reported figure, not a separately audited beneficiary count. The donor is not named in the update.

The gallery preserves the original campaign banner, donor update and carousel cover. These are campaign graphics, not photographs of distribution. The available records do not specify the kit contents, expenditure, distribution date or subsequent educational outcomes; those details have not been inferred.

title: Winter Drive 2025–26
summary: A winter-kit distribution for people in need, with Amaana's impact update reporting 234 kits distributed.
story:
Amaana's Winter Drive 2025–26 provided winter kits to people in need. The campaign's impact update reports 234 kits distributed, each including a sweater or jacket, a blanket and a beanie cap.

The original photographs show the preparation stage: patterned bags arranged together with folded winter items visible inside. No recipients appear in the two selected field photographs. Amaana's separate thank-you update describes many of those reached as madrasah students, orphan children, widows, labourers and domestic workers.

The impact graphic also refers to dates and carpets. Those are distinct activities and are not counted as part of this page's winter-kit result. This page uses Amaana's reported figure and does not infer additional recipients, expenditure or outcomes from the photographs.

title: Dates Distribution 2025
summary: Ramadan dates prepared for community distribution, with Amaana reporting 90 kg distributed in this 2025 edition.
story:
Amaana's 2025 Dates Distribution brought together 90 kg of dates for Ramadan community support. The supplied photographs document the preparation stage: wholesale cartons, individually packed containers and Amaana's Ramadan 1446 Hijri labels.

The photographs show the dates being organized before handover. No recipient total, expenditure figure or list of distribution locations appears in the supplied records, so those details have not been inferred.

The 90 kg quantity is Amaana's campaign-reported figure. This edition is preserved separately from the 2023, 2024 and 2026 drives so each year's evidence remains clear.

title: Meat Distribution Drive 2026

Amaana reports that this edition supported 350 families. This is the campaign-reported reach; the photographs do not provide an independently auditable recipient list or expenditure figure.

One distant identifiable person in the livestock photograph has been deliberately blurred for public display. No additional locations, quantities or outcomes have been inferred from the images.

title: Financial Aid for an Auto-Rickshaw
summary: Livelihood support that funded an auto-rickshaw, with Amaana reporting ₹95,000 raised and the vehicle handed over.
story:
Amaana organised this completed financial-aid appeal to help a young sole breadwinner obtain an auto-rickshaw and build a more dependable livelihood.

The campaign update reports that ₹95,000 was raised. Amaana then assisted with procuring the vehicle, handed it over and provided an additional amount intended to ease the recipient's immediate monthly financial burden.

The photographs document the vehicle and handover. The recipient's face has been deliberately blurred for public display. The archive contains no claim about later earnings, so no longer-term financial outcome has been inferred.

title: Medical Aid for an Eight-Day-Old Baby
summary: Emergency neonatal treatment support, with Amaana reporting ₹1,07,520 raised and handed to the family.
story:
This completed emergency appeal concerned an eight-day-old baby who required oxygen-supported hospital care. The family reported having exhausted its available resources while meeting recent medical costs and caring responsibilities.

The original appeal estimated that a further ₹1.2 lakh would be needed through discharge. Amaana's subsequent update reports that ₹1,07,520 was raised and handed to the family for treatment.

The supplied records do not state the baby's eventual clinical outcome. This archive therefore documents the appeal and financial handover without making a recovery claim.

title: Medical Aid for a Cancer Patient

story:
Amaana organised this medical-aid appeal for a patient reported to have stage-three oral cancer and to need surgery in Hyderabad in May 2025.

The campaign's impact update reports that friends and family contributed ₹3,19,000 and that the amount was handed to the patient's wife. A photograph supplied with the update documents the cash handover.

The concluded appeal's bank account, QR code and payment phone number have been omitted from the public archive. No post-treatment clinical outcome appears in the supplied records, so none has been inferred.

title: Medical Aid for an Ailing Mother
summary: Treatment support for a mother with severe burn injuries, with Amaana reporting ₹72,000 raised and handed to her daughter.
story:
This appeal supported a mother reported to have suffered burns over 45% of her body. Her daughter approached Amaana after the family had already spent ₹4.2 lakh and exhausted its available resources.

Amaana's impact update describes the patient as a single mother of two and reports that ₹72,000 was raised for treatment. The update states that the amount was handed directly to her daughter.

The supplied archive documents the request and handover but does not state a later clinical outcome. This page therefore makes no recovery claim.

title: Medical Aid for Aliza — ARDS
summary: Critical-care support for Aliza during treatment for ARDS, with Amaana reporting ₹4,82,700 raised and handed over.
story:
Amaana opened this medical-aid appeal after Aliza was reported to have developed severe pneumonia that progressed to Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome (ARDS) with refractory hypoxemia. The campaign materials describe escalation from high-frequency ventilation to ECMO and mechanical ventilation in paediatric intensive care.

Amaana's impact update reports that ₹4,82,700 was raised for treatment and that a cheque was handed to the family. A message supplied by Aliza's father acknowledges receipt and thanks donors for their support and prayers.

For public display, Aliza's face has been heavily blurred and the family's phone and contact details have been redacted. The archived donation card and its bank account, QR code and payment phone number are not published. The materials express hope for recovery but do not establish a final clinical outcome, so none is claimed here.

title: Eid Gift Kits 2024
summary: A 467-kit Eid distribution documented in Amaana's 2024 campaign summary and preparation photographs.
story:
Amaana's 2024 edition prepared food kits with staple groceries, cooking ingredients, spices, dry fruits, milk, tea and a cash allowance for meat and curd. The selected images show a representative kit and the completed Amaana-labelled bags.

The supplied summary records 467 kits at ₹1,500 each and total expenditure of ₹710,500 including packaging and transport. These are campaign-reported figures and have not been independently audited.

The public record focuses on the preparation itself. It does not publish beneficiary identities or infer additional recipients from the photographs.

title: Eid Gift Kits 2026
summary: Amaana's 2026 impact graphic reports 710 families supported through the Eid Gift Kits distribution.
story:
Amaana's 2026 Eid Gift Kits edition assembled staple groceries, cooking ingredients, milk, spices and festive foods in individually labelled bags. The photographs document a representative kit, rows of completed bags and transport preparation. The kits were funded through non-Zakat contributions.

Amaana reports 710 families supported: 201 women-led households facing hardship, 134 children and students, 86 masjid-linked beneficiaries, 118 other financially vulnerable households, 65 daily-wage or skilled workers, 55 widows, 33 drivers or transport workers, and 18 people facing medical or disability hardship. The supplied impact graphic has been corrected to these canonical figures. These categories and the overall reach are campaign-reported and have not been independently audited.

No recipient identities are shown in the selected public photographs, and the page does not infer expenditure or additional reach beyond the supplied campaign record.
